attributes.summary: Amoxicillin-clavulanate given despite a penicillin allergy flag; anaphylaxis treated with epinephrine
Critical potassium result communicated later than the policy window
Delay in contact isolation after C. difficile positive result
NSAID prescribed to a patient with CKD, followed by AKI
Missed post-discharge heart-failure follow-up call, followed by readmission

attributes.statement: Critical potassium: 6.2 mmol/L or higher, or 2.9 mmol/L or lower
Sepsis bundle v3 (effective 2026-03-01): first antibiotic within 50 minutes of sepsis alert; v2 (to 2026-02-28) was 60 minutes. Repeat lactate within 2 hours if above 2.5 mmol/L
Metformin: maximum 1,000 mg/day when eGFR 30-44; stop below 30
Pharmacist verification of any new apixaban order within 4 hours
Default warfarin INR target 2.0-3.0; INR above 4.5 triggers anticoagulation-clinic call within 24 hours; INR check within 72 hours of discharge
Heart-failure discharge: phone call within 48 hours and clinic visit within 7 days
Chest-pain pathway: hs-troponin at 0 and 2 hours; ECG within 10 minutes of arrival
Dual verification (pharmacist and nurse) before the first dose of any beta-lactam in a patient with any allergy flag
C. difficile: contact-enteric precautions until 72 hours after diarrhea resolves
IV vancomycin: pharmacy-managed dosing; first level before the fourth dose
DKA infusion transition when beta-hydroxybutyrate is below 0.6 mmol/L on two consecutive checks; hypoglycemia alert threshold below 4.0 mmol/L
Critical results phoned to the responsible clinician within 20 minutes of verification, with read-back
Levothyroxine and oral iron separated by at least 4 hours
